clue.text: Stranded, like Noah on Ararat?

definitions.meaning: left stuck and helpless, with no way out of a situation
the Ark came to rest on Mount Ararat, lofty and with the flood waters gone

explanation.surface: A question comparing someone marooned to Noah when his Ark grounded on the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means left stranded, and literally describes a boat raised up on a mountaintop once the water drained.

clue.text: Introduction to Homer, or magnificent Roman poet

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word Homer is the one taken

parts.note: taken as written
ace is informal praise meaning excellent or magnificent

explanation.surface: Seems to weigh up whether to start with Homer or a great Latin poet instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintus Horatius Flaccus, author of the Odes, was a leading poet of Augustan Rome.

clue.text: Good scope offered by opening on board

parts.note: an ambit is the scope or extent of something

explanation.surface: Reads like praise for the wide possibilities a chess opening gives a player.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a gambit is an opening move sacrificing material for advantage, played on the board.

clue.text: A breeze that may be passing through Tivoli Gardens?

definitions.meaning: something very easy to do, a cinch

definitions.text: that may be passing through Tivoli Gardens?
definitions.meaning: Tivoli Gardens is a park in Copenhagen, so a stroll through it fits literally

explanation.surface: Pictures a light wind blowing through the famous Copenhagen pleasure gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a very easy task; literally it is a stroll through a park such as Tivoli Gardens.

clue.text: Achieve marvellous results? Party is curious to know

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
someone who wonders is curious to know something

explanation.surface: Asks whether a party guest is curious about how great success is achieved.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes producing remarkable effects or improvements, as a tonic that works miracles.

clue.text: Come to religious education supported by a church

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the following ones, held up by them

parts.note: RE is the school-subject abbreviation for religious education

explanation.surface: Suggests religious teaching being propped up by a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place or a figure is to get there, a synonym for come to.

clue.text: Stone in ring friend's put on

indicators.note: in an across entry one piece is added onto the end of the other

parts.note: O is ring-shaped, so ring gives that letter
a pal is a friend; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A friend has slipped on a ring set with a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: This iridescent gem is a semi-precious stone often set in rings.

clue.text: Pushed doctor to appear in red-top needing circulation

indicators.note: the doctor piece shows up inside the other letters
the letters of red-top must be moved around into a new order

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor is to feature in a tabloid newspaper desperate to boost sales.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid, named for its red masthead; 'circulation' looks like newspaper sales but asks for the letters to be stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote something is to push or advertise it, so pushed and promoted are synonyms.

clue.text: Learned line? Say again

parts.note: to iterate is to repeat or say again

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a line to be repeated after learning it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well read and educated can be called learned, a synonym for well-lettered.

clue.text: OK playing violin tune to mass inside

indicators.note: these pieces go within the violin-playing word

parts.note: fiddling is playing the fiddle, a violin
an air is a tune
taken as written
M is the physics abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A musician playing violin, adapting a tune for a church mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means moderately good, middling, just about acceptable.

clue.text: Dance band's leader entering strange area

indicators.note: the leading letter goes into the other pieces

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned British word for odd or strange

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dance band's frontman walks into some odd part of a venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Leading up to concert's finale, playing a tuba, who would you like?

indicators.note: the anagram comes before the final letter in the answer
the words a tuba and who are played around into a new order
the finale of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: At a concert's end, someone with a tuba asks who would like something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' looks like part of the question, but it is fodder for 'playing'; the definition is only the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Offering something with this phrase, as in a suggested drink, is to ask whether someone would like it.

clue.text: Yellow bird

definitions.meaning: the domestic fowl, a farmyard bird

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a canary or other yellow bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a coward, i.e. yellow, and is also the common farm fowl.

clue.text: Hot? Bower provides shelter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
an arbour is a leafy shady bower in a garden

explanation.surface: On a hot day, a garden bower offers some shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A port is a safe place for ships, a haven or shelter from the sea.

clue.text: Complaining, returned post incorrectly delivered

indicators.note: the letters of returned post arrive in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles because their mail was sent back after reaching the wrong address.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something while objecting to it is doing it reluctantly, complaining all the while.

clue.text: Ineffectual, like a team that always loses?

definitions.text: like a team that always loses?
definitions.meaning: a side that never wins scores nothing in a league table

explanation.surface: A dismissive question about a hopeless sports side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means futile or ineffective, and literally a team with zero league points.

clue.text: Old boy's yarn about cold bar

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil, with the 's adding S

indicators.note: the story word goes around the cold letter

parts.note: a yarn is a tale or story
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An old school friend tells a story about a chilly pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is a barrier or hindrance, and so is an impediment in the way.

clue.text: Anticipate number working

parts.note: a figure is a number
on means operating or working, as a machine switched on

explanation.surface: Someone expects a numerical result once the calculation is running.
explanation.definitionFit: To count on or expect something is to anticipate it, an informal phrasal verb.

clue.text: Bishop, agile soul, in play

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
lithe means supple and agile
the spirit is the soul

explanation.surface: Describes a nimble, spiritual bishop as a character on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward's 1941 comedy about a ghostly first wife is a famous play.

clue.text: Pitched, not as a composition for piano, perhaps

indicators.note: pitched means thrown about, so the letters of not as a land in a new order

explanation.surface: Musical talk: a piece judged by its pitch, not as a mere composition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classical form of instrumental piece, frequently written for solo piano.

clue.text: Climb a post in audition?

indicators.note: audition is hearing, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: the word a plus send, a verb for post, said aloud

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about climbing a pole in a stage tryout.
explanation.definitionFit: To go up a slope or a ladder is to climb it.

clue.text: Mutter vaguely about piano and brass instrument

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the piano letter
the letters of mutter are arranged loosely into a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs indistinctly about a piano and a brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaguely' turns MUTTER into TRUMET, and 'about' wraps it round P.
explanation.definitionFit: This valved instrument is a member of the brass family.

clue.text: Dance beat on grand disc

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
O is disc-shaped, so disc gives that letter

explanation.surface: A dance rhythm heard on a terrific record.
explanation.definitionFit: This Argentine ballroom form is a dance.

clue.text: Tiresome outside broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of outside are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A weary verdict on a dull outside broadcast on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is dull and wearisome, the same as boring.

clue.text: Sanction demolition

definitions.meaning: the removal of buildings, as in slum clearing

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for approval to knock down a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means official permission, as security approval, and also the razing of buildings from a site.

clue.text: Picture of island the old lady, for example, brought back

parts.note: the old lady is slang for one's mother, ma

indicators.note: brought back means the example abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: A photo of an island holiday that someone's mother brought home.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a likeness or representation, synonymous with a likeness of someone.

clue.text: Mount from Newmarket, napped

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the words Newmarket napped, running across the gap

explanation.surface: Someone dozed on a horse brought from Newmarket, the English racing town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is a mountain, and mount is used in names of peaks.

clue.text: Got us a card at sea showing a maritime force

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of got us a card are jumbled

explanation.surface: On a voyage someone posted a card to us from the sea patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: This service patrols the shore, enforces sea law and rescues sailors.
